read.name: query_datasource
read.title: Query a datasource
read.description:
Run ONE read-only SELECT on a datasource. The table is named `self` (e.g. `SELECT paese, COUNT(*) AS n FROM self GROUP BY paese ORDER BY n DESC`). Returns columns, rows (capped) and whether the result was truncated.

To answer a question that spans TWO datasources, set `join_datasource_id` to the second one together with `join_left_on` and `join_right_on` (the key columns on each side, comma-separated if the key has several parts). The two are joined before your SQL runs, and `self` is the joined result. `join_how` is inner by default; use left to keep rows that have no match. A column on both sides that is not a key gets the suffix `_right`.

`chart_type` with `chart_x` (the categories) and `chart_y` (the numeric column) draws the result as a chart in the chat; leave them unset otherwise. bar or hbar rank, line or area follow time, pie, donut or treemap show shares, scatter relates two measures, funnel shows stages, waterfall signed steps to a total. combo draws `chart_y2` as a line on its own axis; bullet sets each category's `chart_y` against its target `chart_y2`; heatmap spreads `chart_y` over `chart_x` and the rows in `chart_series`. gauge (one number on a scale up to `chart_max`, target `chart_y2`) and kpi (a headline number; with `chart_x` a period, the last one with its change and trend) need no `chart_x`, and are for when the user asks for an indicator.

write.name: flow_add_source
write.title: Add a source
write.description: Put a datasource in the draft as a source node (an empty source node already there is filled instead). Returns the node id and its columns.

write.name: flow_add_step
write.title: Add a step
write.description:
Add an operation that reads the result of node `after` (and, for join or union, of node `right`). Returns the new node id with its columns and first rows, or the error the preview gave.

Operations and their params (column names are case-sensitive):
- select {columns: [..]} keeps these columns; drop {columns: [..]} removes them; reorder {columns: [..]} puts them first.
- rename {mapping: {old: new}}.
- cast {columns: {col: type}}; types: int, float, str, bool, date, datetime. A value that does not convert becomes null.
- filter {column, operator, value}; operators: eq ne gt ge lt le (one value), in not_in (a list), between ([from, to]), contains starts_with ends_with (text), is_null is_not_null (no value). Numbers as JSON numbers, dates as ISO text ("2024-01-31").
- sort {by: [..], descending: [bool, ..]}: on the first column, then the next ones on equal values; one direction per column (true = descending). Nulls always go last.
- limit {n}. unique {subset?: [..]}. drop_nulls {subset?: [..]}. fill_null {columns: {col: value}}.
- group_by {by: [..], aggregations: [{column, func, alias?}]}; funcs: sum mean min max count median std var first last n_unique.
- pivot {index: [..], on: [..], values: col, func}; unpivot {index?: [..], on?: [..], variable_name?, value_name?}.
- compute {columns: [{name, expr}]}: new or replaced columns from SQL expressions (the SQL dialect of the draft's engine (DuckDB, ClickHouse, Polars SQL…)), applied in order, each may use those before it; window functions with OVER are allowed.
- sql {query}: ONE SELECT ... FROM self in the SQL dialect of the draft's engine (DuckDB, ClickHouse, Polars SQL…); use it only when no operation above fits.
- join {how, on: [..]} or {how, left_on: [..], right_on: [..]}; how: inner left right full semi anti cross. Needs a right input. union {strategy: relaxed|strict} stacks the rows of the right input.

after.description: The node whose result the step reads.

operation.description: One of: select, reorder, drop, rename, cast, filter, sort, limit, unique, fill_null, drop_nulls, group_by, pivot, unpivot, compute, sql, join, union.

right.description: join and union only: the node whose rows they bring in.

write.name: flow_change_step
write.title: Change a step
write.description: Replace the settings of a step (all its params, as flow_add_step takes them; `operation` changes its kind too). Returns its columns and first rows, or the error.

write.name: flow_connect
write.title: Connect two nodes
write.description: Make `to_node` read `from_node` on its left (main) or right (join/union) input, replacing what it read there.

write.name: flow_remove_node
write.title: Remove a node
write.description: Remove a node from the draft. The nodes that read it read what it read instead, so the chain stays connected.

write.name: flow_add_output
write.title: Add an Output
write.description: Add an Output that writes the result of node `after` when the flow runs: a datasource in Tabularia, a database table, a file on S3 or SFTP, or an email with the result attached. Connections are referenced by id (list_connections) and checked as a run checks them — the user's permission, the connection's kind, the domains an SMTP connection may send to. Placeholders such as {date} or {datetime} are allowed in file names, keys and subjects.

timezone.description: The time zone of the dates in the templates (IANA name, default UTC).

after.description: The node whose result the Output writes.

kind.description: What to schedule: flow, datasource (its refresh), sql_script (the write of its datasource) or flow_group.

draft_id.description: flow: a draft whose save is in the plan already (plan_save_flow).

planned_action.description: datasource, sql_script, flow_group: an object this plan creates, which has no id yet — the n of the action that creates it.

write.title: Plan saving a flow
write.description: Add to the plan: save the draft — a new flow is created, a saved one changed (the plan shows what changes). The Outputs it adds or changes are checked again. Planning the same draft again replaces the earlier save. Nothing changes until the plan is confirmed.

write.title: Plan running a flow

draft_id.description: A draft whose save is in the plan already: the flow it makes.

mode.description: development: the flow's editor engine, with its development samples; production: its production engine, every record, as a scheduled run.

write.name: plan_create_datasource
write.title: Plan a new datasource
write.description: Add to the plan: create a datasource that imports from an EXISTING connection — a table or a SQL query of a database, files on S3, SFTP or SharePoint, an HTTP API call. Its first import starts as soon as it is created; plan_schedule (kind datasource, planned_action = this action's n) refreshes it on a schedule. Checked now as the interface checks it: EDIT on the folder, CONNECT on the connection, the name free, the placeholders and the API call checked by the engine. The agent never creates a connection: when the one needed is missing, tell the user. Nothing changes until the plan is confirmed.

of several) — or a RANGE — `day = today-7 .. today step 1d`, the values from

write.name: plan_refresh_datasource
write.title: Plan a refresh
write.description: Add to the plan: refresh a datasource imported from a connection now — it reads its source again and replaces its data when the import succeeds. Nothing runs until the plan is confirmed; then get_run follows the import.

write.name: plan_sql_script
write.title: Plan a SQL script
write.description: Add to the plan: create a SQL script (folder_id, name, sql) or change a saved one (sql_script_id and what changes: the plan shows the difference of the SQL). `output` makes it write its whole result into a datasource: plan_run_sql_script writes it now, plan_schedule (kind sql_script) on a schedule. Checked as the interface checks it — EDIT on the folder, CONNECT on a connection, EDIT on the datasource's folder — and its first rows are read for the plan. Planning the same script again replaces the earlier action. Nothing changes until the plan is confirmed.

sql_script_id.description: A saved script to change; leave it out to create one.

folder_id.description: A new script: its folder (list_folders: can_edit).

name.description: A new script: its name (required). A saved one: a new name.

sql.description: ONE SELECT (or WITH). On the catalog it names datasources by name; on a connection it is the database's own SQL. A new script: required; a saved one: leave it out to keep its SQL.

engine.description: Run on the catalog with this engine (polars, duckdb, chdb, clickhouse, bigquery, as allowed). Leave engine and connection_id out to keep where a saved script runs (a new one: the catalog, the default engine).

connection_id.description: Run on this database connection instead of the catalog (list_connections; the user needs CONNECT).

output.description: The datasource the script writes its whole result into, when plan_run_sql_script or its schedule runs it.

remove_output.description: A saved script: it no longer writes a datasource.

write.name: plan_run_sql_script
write.title: Plan writing a SQL script's datasource
write.description: Add to the plan: run a SQL script once, now, writing its whole result into its datasource (created at the first write, replaced at every one after). Nothing runs until the plan is confirmed; then get_run follows the write.

planned_action.description: A script this plan creates: the n of its plan_sql_script action.

annotations.title: Plan writing a SQL script's datasource

write.name: plan_flow_group
write.title: Plan a flow group
write.description: Add to the plan: create a flow group (folder_id, name, steps) or change a saved one (flow_group_id and what changes: the plan shows which cells come and go). Every cell is checked as the interface checks it: what it runs must be something the user may run (RUN on its folder), a container's image one they may use, a Pushmail's SMTP connection one they may use (CONNECT) with every recipient within its allowed domains. plan_run_flow_group runs it, plan_schedule (kind flow_group) schedules it. Nothing changes until the plan is confirmed.

kind.description: flow: run a flow; refresh: refresh a datasource imported from a connection; script: run a saved Python/R script; sql: write a SQL script's datasource; container: run an image; pushmail: email datasources as .xlsx files and reports as PDF or Excel.

id.description: flow, refresh, script, sql: the object's id. container, pushmail: the cell's number in the group (get_flow_group) to keep it as it is, or to change it with new settings; leave it out for a new one.

write_withheld.name: flow_add_step
write_withheld.title: Add a step
write_withheld.description:
Add an operation that reads the result of node `after` (and, for join or union, of node `right`). Returns the new node id with its columns and first rows, or the error the preview gave.

Operations and their params (column names are case-sensitive):
- select {columns: [..]} keeps these columns; drop {columns: [..]} removes them; reorder {columns: [..]} puts them first.
- rename {mapping: {old: new}}.
- cast {columns: {col: type}}; types: int, float, str, bool, date, datetime. A value that does not convert becomes null.
- filter {column, operator, value}; operators: eq ne gt ge lt le (one value), in not_in (a list), between ([from, to]), contains starts_with ends_with (text), is_null is_not_null (no value). Numbers as JSON numbers, dates as ISO text ("2024-01-31").
- sort {by: [..], descending: [bool, ..]}: on the first column, then the next ones on equal values; one direction per column (true = descending). Nulls always go last.
- limit {n}. unique {subset?: [..]}. drop_nulls {subset?: [..]}. fill_null {columns: {col: value}}.
- group_by {by: [..], aggregations: [{column, func, alias?}]}; funcs: sum mean min max count median std var first last n_unique.
- pivot {index: [..], on: [..], values: col, func}; unpivot {index?: [..], on?: [..], variable_name?, value_name?}.
- compute {columns: [{name, expr}]}: new or replaced columns from SQL expressions (the SQL dialect of the draft's engine (DuckDB, ClickHouse, Polars SQL…)), applied in order, each may use those before it; window functions with OVER are allowed.
- sql {query}: ONE SELECT ... FROM self in the SQL dialect of the draft's engine (DuckDB, ClickHouse, Polars SQL…); use it only when no operation above fits.
- join {how, on: [..]} or {how, left_on: [..], right_on: [..]}; how: inner left right full semi anti cross. Needs a right input. union {strategy: relaxed|strict} stacks the rows of the right input.

This installation is in metadata-only mode: it runs no preview, so it returns neither rows, nor columns, nor the preview's error.

name.description: A new script: its name (required). A saved one: a new name.

sql.description: ONE SELECT (or WITH). On the catalog it names datasources by name; on a connection it is the database's own SQL. A new script: required; a saved one: leave it out to keep its SQL.

engine.description: Run on the catalog with this engine (polars, duckdb, chdb, clickhouse, bigquery, as allowed). Leave engine and connection_id out to keep where a saved script runs (a new one: the catalog, the default engine).

connection_id.description: Run on this database connection instead of the catalog (list_connections; the user needs CONNECT).

output.description: The datasource the script writes its whole result into, when plan_run_sql_script or its schedule runs it.

remove_output.description: A saved script: it no longer writes a datasource.

write_withheld.name: plan_run_sql_script
write_withheld.title: Plan writing a SQL script's datasource
write_withheld.description: Add to the plan: run a SQL script once, now, writing its whole result into its datasource (created at the first write, replaced at every one after). Nothing runs until the plan is confirmed; then get_run follows the write.

planned_action.description: A script this plan creates: the n of its plan_sql_script action.

annotations.title: Plan writing a SQL script's datasource

write_withheld.name: plan_flow_group
write_withheld.title: Plan a flow group
write_withheld.description: Add to the plan: create a flow group (folder_id, name, steps) or change a saved one (flow_group_id and what changes: the plan shows which cells come and go). Every cell is checked as the interface checks it: what it runs must be something the user may run (RUN on its folder), a container's image one they may use, a Pushmail's SMTP connection one they may use (CONNECT) with every recipient within its allowed domains. plan_run_flow_group runs it, plan_schedule (kind flow_group) schedules it. Nothing changes until the plan is confirmed.

kind.description: flow: run a flow; refresh: refresh a datasource imported from a connection; script: run a saved Python/R script; sql: write a SQL script's datasource; container: run an image; pushmail: email datasources as .xlsx files and reports as PDF or Excel.
kind.title: Kind

id.description: flow, refresh, script, sql: the object's id. container, pushmail: the cell's number in the group (get_flow_group) to keep it as it is, or to change it with new settings; leave it out for a new one.
id.title: Id

container.description: container: the settings of a Container node — registryId, repository, tag, command, args, variables [{name, value}], cpu, memory, timeoutSeconds, retries.
container.title: Container

pushmail.description: pushmail: connectionId (an SMTP connection, see list_connections and its allowed_domains), to, cc, subject, body, attachments [{datasourceId, fileName, maxRows}], reports [{reportId, format pdf|xlsx, params {name: value}, fileName, inBody}].

PushmailAttachmentCell.description:
A datasource of a Pushmail cell: its file's name (a template with the Outputs'
placeholders, `.xlsx` added) and the rows it may hold at most.
PushmailAttachmentCell.title: PushmailAttachmentCell

PushmailCell.description:
A Pushmail cell's settings: an email through an SMTP connection, one .xlsx per
datasource and one file per report or dashboard (docs/pushmail.md).
PushmailCell.title: PushmailCell

PushmailDashboardCell.description:
A dashboard of a Pushmail cell (docs/specs/dashboards.md, «Going out»): rendered when the
cell runs, with the rights of whoever runs the group, as a PDF or an image, with these
parameters; its file's name a template with the Outputs' placeholders (the extension added).
PushmailDashboardCell.title: PushmailDashboardCell

PushmailReportCell.description:
A report of a Pushmail cell (docs/specs/reports.md, «Sending»): rendered when the
cell runs, with the rights of whoever runs the group, in its format and with these
parameters; its file's name a template with the Outputs' placeholders (the extension
added). `inBody`: its summary as HTML in the email's body too, under the cell's text
(one report per cell).
PushmailReportCell.title: PushmailReportCell

flow_group_id.description: A saved group to change; leave it out to create one.

folder_id.description: A new group: its folder (list_folders: can_edit).

name.description: A new group: its name (required). A saved one: a new name.

steps.description: The WHOLE grid: a list of steps, each a list of cells run at the same time. A saved group: the new grid (leave it out to keep it).

write_withheld.name: plan_run_flow_group
write_withheld.title: Plan running a flow group
write_withheld.description: Add to the plan: run a flow group once, now — its steps one after another, each cell checked again with the user's rights when it runs. Nothing runs until the plan is confirmed; then get_run follows the run.

planned_action.description: A group this plan creates: the n of its plan_flow_group action.

write_withheld.name: plan_notebook
write_withheld.title: Plan a notebook
write_withheld.description: Add to the plan: create a marimo notebook (folder_id, name, environment_id, source) or change a saved one (notebook_id and what changes: the plan shows the difference of the source). Its app will read data with this user's rights, as the author of the version it runs. Refused while someone has the notebook open in marimo's editor. Only where scripting (Kubernetes) is on. Nothing changes until the plan is confirmed.

notebook_id.description: A saved notebook to change; leave it out to create one.

folder_id.description: A new notebook: its folder (list_folders: can_edit).

name.description: A new notebook: its name (required). A saved one: a new name.

environment_id.description: A Python environment the user may use (list_environments). A new notebook: required.

source.description: The WHOLE marimo file (.py): `import marimo`, `app = marimo.App()`, cells as `@app.cell` functions. Data is read with `import tabularia` and `tabularia.read("Folder/datasource")`. A new notebook: leave it out for a starting one; a saved one: leave it out to keep its source.

write_withheld.name: cancel_plan
write_withheld.title: Cancel a plan
write_withheld.description: Cancel a pending plan: nothing of it will be applied. The drafts stay, to plan again.

plan_id.description: The id a plan tool returned.

write_withheld.name: confirm_plan
write_withheld.title: Apply a plan
write_withheld.description: Apply a pending plan: create, change, run and schedule what it lists, in order, with the user's permissions checked again. Call it ONLY after the user has seen the plan and agreed to it. The first action that fails stops the rest; the result says what was done, with links.

plan_id.description: The id a plan tool returned.
